coverage_exempt.reason: The allocation-null branch sets EDI to zero and immediately dereferences [EDI] at 0x47438e; no normal returning original execution reaches it under the allocator fixture.

Original base constructor 0x4332f0 unconditionally sets bit 9 at 0x4336a9-0x4336d0: count <=9 calls 0x4dbd20(9), whose successful resize rounds count to 32, otherwise count is already >=10. No intervening constructor callee mutates the bitset count. Failed resize faults in 0x4dc680 before returning. Therefore the owned count <=1 branch cannot occur in a valid returning construction.

This branch requires 0x4db6e0 to return zero after failed realloc. Both original paths assign its zero result to EBP at 0x4db70b or 0x4db77f, then call 0x4dc680 at 0x4db788; that helper reads [EBP+4] and faults at address 4 before returning. The failure is reproduced by the original cases check.

A successful first lookup either starts with the index in the signed bounds or resizes 0x4db6e0 to include it. No call or bound store intervenes between the selected-entry check and the second bound check. Thus the second lookup cannot require growth on a valid returning path; the first growth failure faults before returning.

The second growth call is unreachable after a successful first lookup, and a failed 0x4db6e0 realloc would fault in 0x4dc680 reading address 4 before returning zero. This second owned error branch therefore has no valid normal returning original execution.

equivalent_mutants.reason: Only swaps stores/call inside stateSlot growth-failure handling. Original 0x4db6e0 sets EBP to zero on realloc failure then calls 0x4dc680, which faults reading address 4 before returning zero. Both callers have these exact error ranges exempted with original proof; no permitted normal-returning execution enters this block.

Original 0x4747f1 first clears 0x538478. Without growth no call intervenes before second clear at 0x47486a. With successful growth 0x4db6e0 zero-fills each newly added cell (0x4db73a-0x4db755 or 0x4db7ab-0x4db7da), including the selected index; zero callback then takes 0x474866 to base dispatch and bypasses the second clear. Thus reaching the second clear implies the scratch is already zero. Failed growth faults before returning.

limits: SetRectEmpty is a stand-in that clears the supplied rectangle.
InterlockedDecrement is scripted; cases decrement the supplied reference count and return its new value.
notes: Boundary reviewed against all twelve original disassemblies; dispatcher has one cdecl stack argument and constructor __ftol consumes one live x87 operand.
